decision_description: Two Phase 7 budget artifacts for run 9468e1cf-2c71-49e8-91fb-57f6e7192126 contradict on which budget source satisfies gate_09. docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json declares gate_pass_declaration 'pass' via the internal deterministic unit-cost derivation (total EUR 220723.5; every line item Confirmed; unresolved_components empty; blocking_inconsistencies empty), whereas docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json declares 'fail' with blocking inconsistency BI-01 because no lump-sum response is present in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/. The conflicting authorities are Tier 3 (call_binding/selected_call.json, instrument_type = MSCA-PF, a unit-cost instrument) and Tier 4 (the lump-sum-path budget_gate_assessment.json, which presumes an external lump-sum response is required). The specific issue is that the lump-sum external channel is inapplicable to a unit-cost instrument, so a lump-sum 'fail' cannot be the gate-09 authority for MSCA-PF. Resolution: the Tier 3 instrument classification prevails; the internal deterministic unit-cost derivation is the sanctioned budget source and gate_09 is satisfied for this run. The absence of a lump-sum response in received/ is not a blocking failure for an MSCA-PF unit-cost instrument.
alternatives_considered: Treat the Tier 4 lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json 'fail' (BI-01) as authoritative and hard-block Phase 8 — rejected because it misapplies the lump-sum-only external-response requirement to a unit-cost (MSCA-PF) instrument, contradicting the instrument-conditional budget gate established by CLAUDE.md §8.1/§8.4 Amendment C1.

Record the two contradictory declarations as an unresolved conflict and halt for operator resolution — rejected because the constitution resolves the conflict deterministically: for unit-cost instruments the internal deterministic derivation is the sole sanctioned source, and unit_cost_budget.json shows a complete, fully Confirmed derivation with no unresolved or blocking items.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.1 and §8.4 (Amendment C1, instrument-conditional budget gate) — for unit-cost instruments the internal deterministic unit-cost derivation is the sole sanctioned budget source; per the §3 authority hierarchy Tier 3 call_binding/selected_call.json (instrument_type=MSCA-PF) governs over the Tier 4 lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json; §12.3 requires explicit recording of the tier that prevailed and the reasoning.
rationale: Under Amendment C1 the categorical Phase-8 block is preserved and instrument-independent, but the budget source the gate validates is instrument-conditional. MSCA-PF is a unit-cost instrument, so its budget is computed by deterministic derivation (confirmed_months x published_rates x host_country_coefficient), byte-equal replay checked and carrying no judgment. unit_cost_budget.json resolves every component to Confirmed with zero unresolved_components and zero blocking_inconsistencies, satisfying the §8.4 completeness condition for the unit-cost path. The lump-sum external channel (docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner) does not apply to this instrument; the 'fail' recorded in budget_gate_assessment.json presumes a lump-sum-response requirement that C1 scopes to lump-sum instruments only. Selecting that lump-sum 'fail' as authoritative would apply a lump-sum-only rule to a unit-cost instrument and violate the §8.1 sanctioned-source rule and §13.7 (weakening/misapplying gate logic). The contradiction is therefore resolved in favour of the unit-cost derivation, and this determination is written durably to Tier 4 rather than held only in agent memory, per §9.4 and §13.5.
